name: Ehud
bio:
Ehud was the son of Gera, a Benjamite who was left-handed, raised up by the LORD as the judge who delivered Israel from eighteen years of oppression under Eglon, king of Moab.

Under the pretext of delivering tribute to Eglon, Ehud sent his companions away and returned alone, telling the king, "I have a secret message for you." Once the attendants withdrew, Ehud drew a double-edged dagger hidden on his right thigh and drove it into Eglon's belly; he then slipped out, locking the doors behind him, and escaped before the servants discovered their master lying dead (Judges 3:15-25).

Ehud fled and sounded a trumpet call in the hill country of Ephraim, rallying the Israelites and declaring that the LORD had given the Moabites into their hands. He led them to seize the fords of the Jordan, killing about ten thousand Moabites, and the land had rest for eighty years — the longest period of peace recorded in the book of Judges (Judges 3:26-30).
